summary: Remote-controlled PTY execution driven by hardcoded Supabase backend
details: @addai/entity-runtime ships a daemon that polls a hardcoded Supabase project (syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co) for work items and spawns local coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, Gemini, Grok) inside a node-pty pseudo-terminal on the paired host. request-pump.js calls rpc('runtime_pick_next_request',...) and hands each row to session_runner_1.runRequest; claude-spawn.js then invokes pty.spawn(shell, [..., '--dangerously-skip-permissions', '--allowed-tools',..., '--append-system-prompt',...]) using the remote-supplied prompt, working directory, allowed-tools list, and an optional bypass-permissions flag. The dataflow is remote → local PTY: whatever the Supabase backend returns is executed in the installer's shell with the installer's filesystem access, including a mode that disables the agent CLIs' own permission prompts. config.js additionally embeds a static SUPABASE_ANON_KEY JWT for the same project; per Supabase's model the anon role is public by design and gated by RLS, so this key itself is not a credential leak. The remote-controlled PTY channel is present regardless of the package's stated purpose and regardless of user-initiated pairing: control of what runs on the host resides with the backend at syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co / vault.add.ai.
